# Peaking and tapering in an in-season college football schedule

## 1. The question

How should we peak and taper in season? In practice: what a game week looks like as a small taper, how long each quality lasts unexposed, how to read game-week readiness, and what to do in game-free windows (byes, camp to week 1, the postseason).

The sources answer a different question. Every peaking model in the library comes from individual-event sports (kayak, swimming, track and field). **External:** Pyne, Mujika and Reilly 2009 (abstract): taper research does not yet guide a team's league season. **External:** Cuthbert et al. 2024 (PDF p. 5): a season-long peak is unrealistic. No study in two periodization meta-analyses tested whether adaptations peaked when predicted ([[research-papers/afonso-2019-a-systematic-review-of-meta-analyses-comparing-periodized-and-non-periodized-exercise-prog|Afonso 2019]], pp. 1, 4). So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows.

## 2. Bottom line

1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested; no football data]. Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.
2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from Verkhoshansky's 48 h recovery after high-CNS work and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.
3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] Inference: position and starter splits rest on off-season profiles and one exploratory study.
4. Keep aerobic and repeat-effort conditioning every week; it may be lost fastest. [contested: Eric's baseline and Mujika and Padilla 2000 against Issurin]
5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football]

## 3. Where the sources agree

**Cut volume, keep intensity.** Issurin's pre-competitive week cuts volume, keeps frequency and raises the max-speed share ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported], PDF p. 105). **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2003 (abstract): volume down 60 to 90%, frequency down at most 20%. **External:** Bosquet et al. 2007 (abstract; 27 studies, mostly endurance per the evidence file): 2 weeks, volume down 41 to 60%. **External:** Pritchard et al. 2019 (abstract; 11 strength-trained men, 1-week taper, about 70% volume cut): tapers did not differ significantly; only the higher-intensity one showed small effect-size gains in IMTP and FT:CT.

**Strength holds on a small dose.** Issurin, citing Fleck and Kraemer, says team-sport players hold strength 14 to 16 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported], PDF pp. 108-109). **External:** Ronnestad et al. 2011 (abstract; pro soccer, n = 7 per group): one session a week kept strength and 40-m sprint for 12 weeks; one every two weeks lost both; jump height did not change in either group. **External:** Spiering et al. 2021 (abstract; mostly non-athletes) agrees.

**Heavy early, light late.** For a Sunday game, Issurin (citing Baker 2001, rugby league) lifts Tuesday and Wednesday mornings, holds the key practice ("substantial or big" load) Thursday afternoon, and restricts only the pre-game session (Issurin in-season, PDF pp. 108-111). Inference: for Saturday, lifts move to Monday and Tuesday, key practice to Wednesday. **External:** Wellman et al. 2019 (31 D-I players, one program, PDF p. 6): late-season Tuesday and Wednesday loads fell by a planned duration cut; Thursday did not change.

**Strategy metrics beat output.** Jump height fell only slightly by 24 h while RSImod and FT:CT stayed down ([[research-papers/lewis-undated-athlete-monitoring-in-american-collegiate-football|Lewis]], pp. 96-97; n = 5). At 72 h, flight time moved -0.7% and FT:CT -7.7% ([[research-papers/gathercole-2015-alternative-countermovement-jump-analysis-to-quantify-acute-neuromuscular-fatigue|Gathercole 2015]], p. 7; n = 8). The cost is noise: several phase and RFD variables failed reliability ([[research-papers/heishman-2020-countermovement-jump-reliability-performed-with-and-without-an-arm-swing-in-ncaa-division|Heishman 2020]], pp. 5-12). ACWR did no better than an intercept-only model ([[research-papers/impellizzeri-2020-acute-to-random-workload-ratio-is-as-associated-with-injury-as-acute-to-actual-chronic-wor|Impellizzeri 2020]], pp. 4-5).

## 4. Where they disagree

**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday, shifted). Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down about 17% at 72 and 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: lift on incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday. Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours since the game.

**Which quality goes first (D-6).** Issurin: speed (5 ± 3 days) before aerobic and strength (30 ± 5), no sample ([[block-periodization--issurin/claim--residual-training-effect-durations-by-motor-ability|Issurin residuals]] [contested], PDF p. 35). **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic first, speed last. **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2000 (abstract): within 4 weeks, trained athletes lose VO2max fast, strength little. Inference: this sides with class 4. **External:** Saldanha et al. 2026 (abstract; 17 to 21 semi-pro soccer players, uncontrolled): after 5 days off, repeated-sprint time and RAST peak velocity worsened; jump and hip adductor and abductor strength held. Inference: leans toward Issurin, though RAST is not a max-velocity test. Against: **External:** Ross and Leveritt 2001 (PDF p. 17): short-sprint detraining is "less severe than may have been reasonably anticipated". **External:** Bosquet et al. 2013 (abstract; 103 studies): cessation cut maximal power least. Ronnestad kept sprint without max-velocity work. The residual entry notes these may measure cessation versus a retention dose; Issurin calls residual-only design "extremely rigid and inflexible" ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--prolonging-residual-effects-with-mini-blocks|Issurin mini-blocks]] [supported], PDF p. 127). Settle with our data around byes and winter break.

**Lifting near competition (D-5, D-7).** Platonov and Fesenko say it hurts technique; Bompa and Carrera say it keeps force (Issurin pre-competitive, PDF p. 108). **External:** Pritchard et al. 2015 (abstract): 2 to 4 days of training cessation looks optimal for peak strength. Inference: football never stops training, so this only bounds the last lift; the shifted Issurin week puts it 4 days out.

**Maintain or build.** Ronnestad and Spiering maintain on one session; Issurin uses two. **External:** Hoffman et al. 2003 (abstract; freshmen, n = 14 per group, 2 sessions a week): a linear program raised 1RM squat 13.8 ± 7.4 kg, a nonlinear one did not; the abstract garbles one program. Inference: building may suit low-snap freshmen, not starters.

**Timing models.** [[periodization--bompa/principle--supercompensation-cycle|Bompa]] [supported], [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/claim--adaptive-reconstruction-vs-supercompensation|Verkhoshansky]] [contested] and [[elite-sports-performance--evans/claim--fitness-fatigue-model-is-unvalidated-concept|Evans]] [untested] disagree on whether adaptation timing is predictable. Inference: mental models, not a clock.

## 5. What transfers and what does not

**Transfers:** residual direction and weekly re-exposure; the two-mini-block week as a template; keep intensity, cut volume; CMJ strategy metrics. Body mass is not a taper marker: fat mass rose 4.3% at stable mass over 2 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--realization-mesocycle-taper-prescription|Issurin realization]] [supported], PDF pp. 126-127; triathletes, n = 16, no significance test).

**The exception, a bowl.** **External:** Marrier et al. 2017 (abstract; 10 rugby sevens players, 3-week taper): 70 to 80% of peaks fell in the first 2 weeks. **External:** Vachon et al. 2021 (abstract; 14 team-sport studies): moderate gains in power, change of direction and VO2max; no best strategy. **External:** Haugen et al. 2019 (PDF p. 11): 2 to 3 weeks for strength and power sports; smaller gains in sprinters. Fitz-Clarke 1991 finds usual tapers "may be too rigorous and short" ([[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--fitness-fatigue-modeling-and-taper-timing|Verkhoshansky taper]] [supported]). Inference: 1 to 3 weeks, speed and heavy lifting kept, not judged by sprint times alone.

## 6. What none of them covers

- **Bye weeks.** **External:** Peterson (dissertation, unverified year; 108 D-I players) found a group x time interaction on a CMJ stretch-shortening factor: the gap between big and skill or mid-size players widened after the bye and lasted past the next game (PDF p. 52). - **Postseason.** Bowl structure is Inference from kayak calendars; after a long layoff, rebuild contact over 3 to 4 weeks ([[research-papers/stokes-2020-returning-to-play-after-prolonged-training-restrictions-in-professional-collision-sports|Stokes 2020]], p. 7; expert opinion).

- **Course baseline (HHPR 5355, speaker unconfirmed):** speed every 5 days, aerobic and strength every 30 (class-1 p. 27). These are Issurin's Table 1.6 reproduced in the slides (week1-lecture p. 66), not independent support, and class-1 also says aerobic is gained and lost quickly (pp. 25, 28). The real disagreement is class-4 p. 47 against Issurin.
- **Course baseline (HHPR 5355, speaker unconfirmed):** "maintain intensity, reduce volume", a strength retention dose, a waved week (class-1 pp. 17-25; class-8 p. 21). Agrees with section 3.

## 8. Questions for Eric

1. In a 12-plus game season, does "peak" mean every Saturday, target games, or only the postseason?
2. Issurin's Saturday week lifts Monday and Tuesday, 48 and 72 h post-game, while fast force is still down. Where do our heaviest lifts and practice sit, and should heavy and high-velocity work wait until Wednesday?

# Peaking and tapering in an in-season college football schedule

## 1. The question

How should we peak and taper in season? In practice: what a game week looks like as a small taper, how long each quality lasts unexposed, how to read game-week readiness, and what to do in game-free windows (byes, camp to week 1, the postseason).

The sources answer a different question. Every peaking model in the library comes from individual-event sports (kayak, swimming, track and field). **External:** Pyne, Mujika and Reilly 2009 (abstract): taper research does not yet guide a team's league season. **External:** Cuthbert et al. 2024 (PDF p. 5): a season-long peak is unrealistic. No study in two periodization meta-analyses tested whether adaptations peaked when predicted ([[research-papers/afonso-2019-a-systematic-review-of-meta-analyses-comparing-periodized-and-non-periodized-exercise-prog|Afonso 2019]], pp. 1, 4). So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows.

## 2. Bottom line

1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested; no football data]. Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.
2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from Verkhoshansky's 48 h recovery after high-CNS work and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.
3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] Inference: position and starter splits rest on off-season profiles and one exploratory study.
4. Keep aerobic and repeat-effort conditioning every week; it may be lost fastest. [contested: Eric's baseline and Mujika and Padilla 2000 against Issurin]
5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football]

## 3. Where the sources agree

**Cut volume, keep intensity.** Issurin's pre-competitive week cuts volume, keeps frequency and raises the max-speed share ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported], PDF p. 105). **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2003 (abstract): volume down 60 to 90%, frequency down at most 20%. **External:** Bosquet et al. 2007 (abstract; 27 studies, mostly endurance per the evidence file): 2 weeks, volume down 41 to 60%. **External:** Pritchard et al. 2019 (abstract; 11 strength-trained men, 1-week taper, about 70% volume cut): tapers did not differ significantly; only the higher-intensity one showed small effect-size gains in IMTP and FT:CT.

**Strength holds on a small dose.** Issurin, citing Fleck and Kraemer, says team-sport players hold strength 14 to 16 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported], PDF pp. 108-109). **External:** Ronnestad et al. 2011 (abstract; pro soccer, n = 7 per group): one session a week kept strength and 40-m sprint for 12 weeks; one every two weeks lost both; jump height did not change in either group. **External:** Spiering et al. 2021 (abstract; mostly non-athletes) agrees.

**Heavy early, light late.** For a Sunday game, Issurin (citing Baker 2001, rugby league) lifts Tuesday and Wednesday mornings, holds the key practice ("substantial or big" load) Thursday afternoon, and restricts only the pre-game session (Issurin in-season, PDF pp. 108-111). Inference: for Saturday, lifts move to Monday and Tuesday, key practice to Wednesday. **External:** Wellman et al. 2019 (31 D-I players, one program, PDF p. 6): late-season Tuesday and Wednesday loads fell by a planned duration cut; Thursday did not change.

**Strategy metrics beat output.** Jump height fell only slightly by 24 h while RSImod and FT:CT stayed down ([[research-papers/lewis-undated-athlete-monitoring-in-american-collegiate-football|Lewis]], pp. 96-97; n = 5). At 72 h, flight time moved -0.7% and FT:CT -7.7% ([[research-papers/gathercole-2015-alternative-countermovement-jump-analysis-to-quantify-acute-neuromuscular-fatigue|Gathercole 2015]], p. 7; n = 8). The cost is noise: several phase and RFD variables failed reliability ([[research-papers/heishman-2020-countermovement-jump-reliability-performed-with-and-without-an-arm-swing-in-ncaa-division|Heishman 2020]], pp. 5-12). ACWR did no better than an intercept-only model ([[research-papers/impellizzeri-2020-acute-to-random-workload-ratio-is-as-associated-with-injury-as-acute-to-actual-chronic-wor|Impellizzeri 2020]], pp. 4-5).

## 4. Where they disagree

**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday, shifted). Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down about 17% at 72 and 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: lift on incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday. Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours since the game.

**Which quality goes first (D-6).** Issurin: speed (5 ± 3 days) before aerobic and strength (30 ± 5), no sample ([[block-periodization--issurin/claim--residual-training-effect-durations-by-motor-ability|Issurin residuals]] [contested], PDF p. 35). **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic first, speed last. **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2000 (abstract): within 4 weeks, trained athletes lose VO2max fast, strength little. Inference: this sides with class 4. **External:** Saldanha et al. 2026 (abstract; 17 to 21 semi-pro soccer players, uncontrolled): after 5 days off, repeated-sprint time and RAST peak velocity worsened; jump and hip adductor and abductor strength held. Inference: leans toward Issurin, though RAST is not a max-velocity test. Against: **External:** Ross and Leveritt 2001 (PDF p. 17): short-sprint detraining is "less severe than may have been reasonably anticipated". **External:** Bosquet et al. 2013 (abstract; 103 studies): cessation cut maximal power least. Ronnestad kept sprint without max-velocity work. The residual entry notes these may measure cessation versus a retention dose; Issurin calls residual-only design "extremely rigid and inflexible" ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--prolonging-residual-effects-with-mini-blocks|Issurin mini-blocks]] [supported], PDF p. 127). Settle with our data around byes and winter break.

**Lifting near competition (D-5, D-7).** Platonov and Fesenko say it hurts technique; Bompa and Carrera say it keeps force (Issurin pre-competitive, PDF p. 108). **External:** Pritchard et al. 2015 (abstract): 2 to 4 days of training cessation looks optimal for peak strength. Inference: football never stops training, so this only bounds the last lift; the shifted Issurin week puts it 4 days out.

**Maintain or build.** Ronnestad and Spiering maintain on one session; Issurin uses two. **External:** Hoffman et al. 2003 (abstract; freshmen, n = 14 per group, 2 sessions a week): a linear program raised 1RM squat 13.8 ± 7.4 kg, a nonlinear one did not; the abstract garbles one program. Inference: building may suit low-snap freshmen, not starters.

**Timing models.** [[periodization--bompa/principle--supercompensation-cycle|Bompa]] [supported], [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/claim--adaptive-reconstruction-vs-supercompensation|Verkhoshansky]] [contested] and [[elite-sports-performance--evans/claim--fitness-fatigue-model-is-unvalidated-concept|Evans]] [untested] disagree on whether adaptation timing is predictable. Inference: mental models, not a clock.

## 5. What transfers and what does not

**Transfers:** residual direction and weekly re-exposure; the two-mini-block week as a template; keep intensity, cut volume; CMJ strategy metrics. Body mass is not a taper marker: fat mass rose 4.3% at stable mass over 2 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--realization-mesocycle-taper-prescription|Issurin realization]] [supported], PDF pp. 126-127; triathletes, n = 16, no significance test).

**Does not transfer:** single-peak prescriptions (1 to 3 week realization, kayak dosages, 4 to 12 week delayed gains per Siff and Verkhoshansky, cited by [[periodization--bompa/principle--concentrated-loading-overreaching|Bompa]] [supported], the 3% taper gain) assume one target event.

**The exception, a bowl.** **External:** Marrier et al. 2017 (abstract; 10 rugby sevens players, 3-week taper): 70 to 80% of peaks fell in the first 2 weeks. **External:** Vachon et al. 2021 (abstract; 14 team-sport studies): moderate gains in power, change of direction and VO2max; no best strategy. **External:** Haugen et al. 2019 (PDF p. 11): 2 to 3 weeks for strength and power sports; smaller gains in sprinters. Fitz-Clarke 1991 finds usual tapers "may be too rigorous and short" ([[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--fitness-fatigue-modeling-and-taper-timing|Verkhoshansky taper]] [supported]). Inference: 1 to 3 weeks, speed and heavy lifting kept, not judged by sprint times alone.

## 6. What none of them covers

- **Bye weeks.** **External:** Peterson (dissertation, unverified year; 108 D-I players) found a group x time interaction on a CMJ stretch-shortening factor: the gap between big and skill or mid-size players widened after the bye and lasted past the next game (PDF p. 52). Within-group change is not tested there. Inference: dose byes by position and keep a speed or repeated-sprint exposure, given Saldanha.
- **Short weeks, camp to week 1, position groups, low-snap players.** Only descriptive or off-population data: [[research-papers/galiano-2026-more-matches-less-time-how-load-ratios-reveal-gaps-between-training-and-competition-in-foo|Galiano 2026]], [[research-papers/claudino-2016-autoregulating-jump-performance-to-induce-functional-overreaching|Claudino 2016]], [[research-papers/merrigan-2022-comparisons-of-countermovement-jump-force-time-characteristics-among-national-collegiate-a|Merrigan 2022]], [[research-papers/lever-2026-game-exposure-shapes-intensity-and-performance-in-division-i-college-football|Lever 2026]], and [[research-papers/aychman-2026-multimodal-indicators-of-non-functional-overreaching-in-ncaa-division-i-american-football|Aychman 2026]] (non-starters recovered worse on lower load; one program, exploratory, pp. 1, 9).
- **Postseason.** Bowl structure is Inference from kayak calendars; after a long layoff, rebuild contact over 3 to 4 weeks ([[research-papers/stokes-2020-returning-to-play-after-prolonged-training-restrictions-in-professional-collision-sports|Stokes 2020]], p. 7; expert opinion).
- **Season-long detraining.** Only the 14 to 16 week figure and Hoffman 2003; nothing on starters' speed.

Would fill: Bompa Ch 7, Issurin Ch 4; others in the evidence map, Gaps.

## 7. Eric's baseline

- **Eric's baseline:** daily CMJ mRSI is the readiness marker, "objective, consistent, and actionable" (SportSmith piece); wellness surveys were dropped after athletes gamed them. Inference: matches section 3 and [[research-papers/mccall-2023-a-qualitative-study-of-11-world-class-team-sport-athletes-experiences-answering-subjective|McCall 2023]].
- **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic is lost fastest, speed slowest; that order sets re-exposure. Conflicts with Issurin.
- **Course baseline (HHPR 5355, speaker unconfirmed):** speed every 5 days, aerobic and strength every 30 (class-1 p. 27). These are Issurin's Table 1.6 reproduced in the slides (week1-lecture p. 66), not independent support, and class-1 also says aerobic is gained and lost quickly (pp. 25, 28). The real disagreement is class-4 p. 47 against Issurin.
- **Course baseline (HHPR 5355, speaker unconfirmed):** "maintain intensity, reduce volume", a strength retention dose, a waved week (class-1 pp. 17-25; class-8 p. 21). Agrees with section 3.
- **Eric's baseline (class-4 slides, pp. 34, 39):** conditioning targets alactic and aerobic capacity. Inference: fits the 1:7 ratio in 2004 D-I games ([[research-papers/iosia-2008-analysis-of-exercise-to-rest-ratios-during-division-ia-televised-football-competition|Iosia 2008]]).

## 8. Questions for Eric

1. In a 12-plus game season, does "peak" mean every Saturday, target games, or only the postseason?
2. Issurin's Saturday week lifts Monday and Tuesday, 48 and 72 h post-game, while fast force is still down. Where do our heaviest lifts and practice sit, and should heavy and high-velocity work wait until Wednesday?
3. Class-4 (p. 47) says aerobic is lost fastest; the course's 5 and 30 day figures are Issurin's table, and class-1 says aerobic goes quickly too. Is class-4 your view, and are the course in-season rules yours?
4. How are bye weeks used now (restoration, loading, or a speed and strength top-up), and by position?
5. Which mRSI drop, on which day, changes the plan, and do linemen and low-snap players get their own thresholds?
6. Does the postseason get a distinct 1 to 3 week taper or the normal game week?

The sources answer a different question. Every peaking model in the library comes from individual-event sports (kayak, swimming, track and field). **External:** Pyne, Mujika and Reilly 2009 (abstract): taper research does not yet guide a team's league season. **External:** Cuthbert et al. 2024 (PDF p. 5): a season-long peak is unrealistic. So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows.

lines: ## 4. Where they disagree

-**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday, shifted). Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down about 17% at 72 and 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: lift on incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday. Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours since the game.

Ronnestad kept sprint without max-velocity work. 27	## 2. Bottom line
28	
29	1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested; no football data]. Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.
30	2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from Verkhoshansky's 48 h recovery after high-CNS work and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.
31	3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] Inference: position and starter splits rest on off-season profiles and one exploratory study.
32	4. Keep aerobic and repeat-effort conditioning every week; it may be lost fastest. [contested: Eric's baseline and Mujika and Padilla 2000 against Issurin]
33	5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football]
34	
35	## 3. Where the sources agree
36	
37	**Cut volume, keep intensity.** Issurin's pre-competitive week cuts volume, keeps frequency and raises the max-speed share ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported], PDF p. 105). **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2003 (abstract): volume down 60 to 90%, frequency down at most 20%. **External:** Bosquet et al. 2007 (abstract; 27 studies, mostly endurance per the evidence file): 2 weeks, volume down 41 to 60%. **External:** Pritchard et al. 2019 (abstract; 11 strength-trained men, 1-week taper, about 70% volume cut): tapers did not differ significantly; only the higher-intensity one showed small effect-size gains in IMTP and FT:CT.
38

41	**Heavy early, light late.** For a Sunday game, Issurin (citing Baker 2001, rugby league) lifts Tuesday and Wednesday mornings, holds the key practice ("substantial or big" load) Thursday afternoon, and restricts only the pre-game session (Issurin in-season, PDF pp. 108-111). ## 1. The question

How should we peak and taper in season? It splits into the game week as a small taper, how long qualities last unexposed, game-week readiness, and game-free windows (byes, camp to week 1, postseason).

The sources answer a different question: every peaking model in the library comes from individual-event sports (kayak, swimming, track and field). **External:** Pyne, Mujika and Reilly 2009 (abstract): taper research does not yet guide a league season. **External:** Cuthbert et al. 2024 (PDF p. 5): a season-long peak is unrealistic. No study in two periodization meta-analyses tested whether adaptations peaked when predicted ([[research-papers/afonso-2019-a-systematic-review-of-meta-analyses-comparing-periodized-and-non-periodized-exercise-prog|Afonso 2019]], pp. 1, 4). So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows.

## 2. Bottom line

1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested; no football data]. Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.
2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from Verkhoshansky's 48 h recovery after high-CNS work and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.
3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] Inference: position and starter splits rest on off-season profiles and one exploratory study.
4. Keep aerobic and repeat-effort conditioning every week; it may be lost fastest. [contested: Eric's baseline and Mujika and Padilla 2000 against Issurin]
5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football]

## 3. Where the sources agree

**Cut volume, keep intensity.** Issurin's pre-competitive week cuts volume, keeps frequency and raises the max-speed share ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported], PDF p. 105). **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2003 (abstract): volume down 60 to 90%, frequency down at most 20%. **External:** Bosquet et al. 2007 (abstract; 27 studies, mostly endurance per the evidence file): 2 weeks, volume down 41 to 60%. **External:** Pritchard et al. 2019 (abstract; 11 strength-trained men, 1-week taper, about 70% volume cut): tapers did not differ significantly; only the higher-intensity one showed small effect-size gains in IMTP and FT:CT.

**Strength holds on a small dose.** Issurin, citing Fleck and Kraemer, says team-sport players hold strength 14 to 16 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported], PDF pp. 108-109). **External:** Ronnestad et al. 2011 (abstract; pro soccer, n = 7 per group): one session a week kept strength and 40-m sprint for 12 weeks; one every two weeks lost both; jump height did not change in either group. **External:** Spiering et al. 2021 (abstract; mostly non-athletes) agrees.

**Heavy early, light late.** For a Sunday game, Issurin (citing Baker 2001, rugby league) lifts Tuesday and Wednesday mornings, holds the key practice ("substantial or big" load) Thursday afternoon, and restricts only the pre-game session (Issurin in-season, PDF pp. 108-111). Inference: for Saturday, lifts move to Monday and Tuesday, key practice to Wednesday. **External:** Wellman et al. 2019 (31 D-I players, one program, PDF p. 6): late-season Tuesday and Wednesday loads fell by a planned duration cut; Thursday did not change.

**Strategy metrics beat output.** Jump height fell only slightly by 24 h while RSImod and FT:CT stayed down ([[research-papers/lewis-undated-athlete-monitoring-in-american-collegiate-football|Lewis]], pp. 96-97; n = 5). At 72 h, flight time moved -0.7% and FT:CT -7.7% ([[research-papers/gathercole-2015-alternative-countermovement-jump-analysis-to-quantify-acute-neuromuscular-fatigue|Gathercole 2015]], p. 7; n = 8). The cost is noise: several phase and RFD variables failed reliability ([[research-papers/heishman-2020-countermovement-jump-reliability-performed-with-and-without-an-arm-swing-in-ncaa-division|Heishman 2020]], pp. 5-12). ACWR did no better than an intercept-only model ([[research-papers/impellizzeri-2020-acute-to-random-workload-ratio-is-as-associated-with-injury-as-acute-to-actual-chronic-wor|Impellizzeri 2020]], pp. 4-5).

## 4. Where they disagree

**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday, shifted). Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down about 17% at 72 and 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). Ronnestad kept sprint without max-velocity work. The residual entry notes these may measure cessation versus a retention dose; Issurin calls residual-only design "extremely rigid and inflexible" ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--prolonging-residual-effects-with-mini-blocks|Issurin mini-blocks]] [supported], PDF p. 127). Settle with our data around byes and winter break.

**Lifting near competition (D-5, D-7).** Platonov and Fesenko say it hurts technique; Bompa and Carrera say it keeps force (Issurin pre-competitive, PDF p. 108). **External:** Pritchard et al. 2015 (abstract): 2 to 4 days of training cessation looks optimal for peak strength. Inference: football never stops training, so this only bounds the last lift; the shifted Issurin week puts it 4 days out.

**Maintain or build.** Ronnestad and Spiering maintain on one session; Issurin uses two. **External:** Hoffman et al. 2003 (abstract, partly garbled; freshmen, n = 14 per group, 2 sessions a week): linear training raised 1RM squat 13.8 ± 7.4 kg, nonlinear did not. Inference: building may suit low-snap freshmen.

Inference: mental models, not a clock.

Fitz-Clarke 1991 finds usual tapers "may be too rigorous and short" ([[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--fitness-fatigue-modeling-and-taper-timing|Verkhoshansky taper]] [supported]). Inference: 1 to 3 weeks, speed and heavy lifting kept, not judged by sprint times alone.

## 6. What none of them covers

## 7. Eric's baseline

- **Eric's baseline:** daily CMJ mRSI is the readiness marker, "objective, consistent, and actionable" (SportSmith piece); athletes gamed wellness surveys. These are Issurin's Table 1.6 reproduced in the slides (week1-lecture p. 66), not independent support, and class-1 also says aerobic is gained and lost quickly (pp. 25, 28). The real disagreement is class-4 p. 47 against Issurin.

Within-group change is not tested there. Inference: dose byes by position and keep a speed or repeated-sprint exposure, given Saldanha.

- **Postseason.** Bowl structure is Inference from kayak calendars; after a long layoff, rebuild contact over 3 to 4 weeks ([[research-papers/stokes-2020-returning-to-play-after-prolonged-training-restrictions-in-professional-collision-sports|Stokes 2020]], p. 7; expert opinion).

lines: **Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday, shifted). Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down 17.8% at 72 h and 16.9% at 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: load incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday? Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours post-game.

lines: How should we peak and taper in season? It splits into the game week as a small taper, how long qualities last unexposed, game-week readiness, and game-free windows (byes, camp to week 1, postseason).

-The sources answer a different question: every peaking model in the library comes from individual-event sports (kayak, swimming, track and field). **External:** Pyne, Mujika and Reilly 2009 (abstract): taper research does not yet guide a league season. **External:** Cuthbert et al. 2024 (PDF p. 5): a season-long peak is unrealistic. No study in two periodization meta-analyses tested whether adaptations peaked when predicted ([[research-papers/afonso-2019-a-systematic-review-of-meta-analyses-comparing-periodized-and-non-periodized-exercise-prog|Afonso 2019]], pp. 1, 4). So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows.

lines: ## 4. Where they disagree

-**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday, shifted). Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down 17.8% at 72 h and 16.9% at 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: load incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday? Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours post-game.

+**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday if shifted for Saturday, Inference). **External:** Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down 17.8% at 72 h and 16.9% at 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: load incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday? Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours post-game.

**Which quality goes first (D-6).** Issurin: speed (5 ± 3 days) before aerobic and strength (30 ± 5), no sample ([[block-periodization--issurin/claim--residual-training-effect-durations-by-motor-ability|Issurin residuals]] [contested], PDF p. 35). **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic first, speed last. **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2000 (abstract): within 4 weeks, trained athletes lose VO2max fast, strength little. Inference: sides with class 4. **External:** Saldanha et al. 2026 (abstract; 17 to 21 semi-pro soccer players, uncontrolled): after 5 days off, repeated-sprint time and RAST peak velocity worsened; jump and hip adductor and abductor strength held. Inference: leans toward Issurin, though RAST is not a max-velocity test. Against: **External:** Ross and Leveritt 2001 (PDF p. 17): short-sprint detraining is "less severe than may have been reasonably anticipated". **External:** Bosquet et al. 2013 (abstract; 103 studies): cessation cut maximal power least. Ronnestad kept sprint without max-velocity work. The residual entry notes these may measure cessation versus a retention dose; Issurin calls residual-only design "extremely rigid and inflexible" ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--prolonging-residual-effects-with-mini-blocks|Issurin mini-blocks]] [supported], PDF p. 127). Settle with our data around byes and winter break.

-**Heavy early, light late.** For a Sunday game, Issurin (citing Baker 2001, rugby league) lifts Tuesday and Wednesday mornings, holds the key practice ("substantial or big" load) Thursday afternoon, and restricts only the pre-game session (Issurin in-season, PDF pp. 108-111). Inference: for Saturday, lifts move to Monday and Tuesday, key practice to Wednesday. **External:** Wellman et al. 2019 (31 D-I players, one program, PDF p. 6): late-season Tuesday and Wednesday loads fell by a planned duration cut; Thursday did not change.

**Strategy metrics beat output.** Jump height fell only slightly by 24 h while RSImod and FT:CT stayed down ([[research-papers/lewis-undated-athlete-monitoring-in-american-collegiate-football|Lewis]], pp. 96-97; n = 5). lines: ## 2. Bottom line

1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested; no football data]. Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.

-2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from Verkhoshansky's 48 h recovery after high-CNS work and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.

+2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--central-vs-peripheral-fatigue-mechanisms|Verkhoshansky's]] [supported] 48 h recovery after high-CNS work (printed p. 15) and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.

3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] Inference: position and starter splits rest on off-season profiles and one exploratory study.
4. Keep aerobic and repeat-effort conditioning every week; it may be lost fastest. [contested: Eric's baseline and Mujika and Padilla 2000 against Issurin]
5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football]
